_**User**_

You are setting up the foundational repository for Innerflect’s operational intelligence system.

Your job is to create a clean, scalable, highly navigable documentation and prompt repository that will become the backbone of how Innerflect works across development, marketing, branding, sales, project management, and operations.

This is not just a prompt dump.
This must become a real operating system that is:
- easy to use in GitHub
- easy to navigate in Markdown
- easy to render as a clean HTML documentation site
- clear for a team
- highly structured
- reusable
- versionable
- consistent
- visually and logically coherent

==================================================
PRIMARY GOAL
==================================================

Create the first version of an “Innerflect Ops” repository with:

1. A strong repository structure
2. Excellent documentation architecture
3. A prompt/playbook system
4. Clear taxonomy for all files
5. Reusable templates
6. Easy navigation in both GitHub and docs-site format
7. Documentation standards for future additions
8. A setup ready for long-term team use

==================================================
HIGH-LEVEL REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

The repository must:

- Be Markdown-first
- Be documentation-centric
- Be optimized for both GitHub browsing and static HTML docs rendering
- Be readable by humans and useful for AI-assisted workflows
- Avoid duplication and prompt chaos
- Use consistent naming conventions
- Make it easy to find the right prompt/playbook fast
- Be organized around operating logic, not random categories
- Be easy to extend later

==================================================
DOCUMENTATION STRATEGY
==================================================

Implement the repository so that it supports:

- clean README-based GitHub navigation
- a docs structure that can later be rendered in Docusaurus
- autogenerated or easily maintained sidebars
- structured pages with consistent frontmatter
- strong internal linking between related documents
- HTML-friendly formatting
- clear section landing pages / index pages

Documentation must be:
- simple to scan
- cleanly nested
- no deep chaotic folder trees
- no vague file names
- no giant messy documents

Every main folder must have its own index.md or README.md that explains:
- what that section is
- when to use it
- what files exist inside
- how to choose the right file

==================================================
WHAT EACH MAJOR AREA SHOULD CONTAIN
==================================================

1. GOVERNANCE
Create docs that define:
- mission of the repo
- how Innerflect uses prompts
- versioning logic
- naming conventions
- contribution rules
- how to add a new playbook
- how to archive old prompts
- how to avoid duplication

2. CORE RULES
Create reusable rules documents for:
- development standards
- design standards
- documentation standards
- research standards
- QA standards
- Git/GitHub standards
- communication standards

4. TEMPLATES
Create templates for:

5. CHECKLISTS
Create checklists for:
- new project setup
- docs quality review
- prompt quality review
- repo health review
- project continuation
- release readiness

6. EXAMPLES
Create a small examples section showing:
- example of a good playbook
- example of a bad prompt vs good playbook structure
- example of a clean audit output
- example of a reusable research output

==================================================
PLAYBOOK FILE FORMAT
==================================================

Every playbook must follow the same structure:

- Title
- Purpose
- When to use
- Inputs required
- Step-by-step execution logic
- The actual Cursor prompt
- Expected output
- Quality checks
- Common failure modes
- Related documents

Make sure every playbook is operationally useful, not generic.

==================================================
DOCUMENT DESIGN RULES
==================================================

Use these rules:

- Short paragraphs
- Strong headings
- Clear section hierarchy
- Bullet points only when useful
- No bloated intros
- No vague words like “misc”, “other”, “stuff”
- File names must be descriptive and kebab-case
- Every folder must be self-explanatory
- Avoid more than 3 levels of nesting unless truly needed
- Every page should help a team member quickly decide whether they are in the right place

==================================================
HTML / DOCS SITE REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Prepare the docs folder so it can be used for a future Docusaurus documentation site.

Create:
- docs/index.md
- category landing pages
- beginner-friendly “how to use this repo”
- an information architecture that will render cleanly as HTML
- strong internal links
- a docs sidebar proposal file

Also create:
- docusaurus-recommendation.md
explaining how this repo should later be rendered as a docs site, including:
- why Docusaurus is recommended
- what structure already supports it
- what would be needed later to activate it

==================================================
README REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Create a high-quality root README.md that includes:

- what this repo is
- who it is for
- the core philosophy
- how the repo is structured
- how to use it
- how to find the right playbook
- how to contribute
- where to start first

This README must be clean, premium, and easy to scan.

==================================================
AGENTS REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Create an AGENTS.md file that defines the operational behavior for AI-assisted work in this repository.

It should include:
- act research-first
- prioritize reuse over recreation
- no duplication
- maintain docs when system changes
- prefer existing templates and structures
- preserve naming conventions
- improve clarity, not complexity
- keep outputs team-usable
- use evidence-based reasoning in research files
- identify assumptions and unknowns

==================================================
OUTPUT INSTRUCTIONS
==================================================

Do not just describe the structure.

Actually generate:
- the folder tree
- the content of the most important files
- placeholders for the rest
- all initial index pages
- the root README
- AGENTS.md
- the main template files
- the first example playbooks

Where full file creation would be too long, create:
- strong skeleton files
- consistent headings
- meaningful placeholder text
- TODO markers only where needed

==================================================
IMPORTANT QUALITY BAR
==================================================

This must feel like the beginning of a serious internal operating system.

It should feel:
- premium
- coherent
- calm
- intelligent
- extensible
- non-chaotic
- immediately usable

Do not make it look like a random starter repo.
Do not create shallow filler text.
Do not produce generic AI-slop prompts.

Make decisions that reduce long-term entropy.

At the end, provide:
1. the final proposed folder tree
2. the contents of the key files
3. the recommended next 10 files to write in full
4. suggestions for what should later become Cursor Rules, Skills, Subagents, and MCP guides

I'll replace matchesGlob with: 
```
function fileMatches(rel, includeGlobs) {
  const ext = path.extname(rel).toLowerCase();
  const allowed = [".md", ".mdx", ".tsx", ".jsx", ".vue", ".html"];
  if (!includeGlobs.length) return allowed.includes(ext);
  return includeGlobs.some(g => {
    if (g.includes("*.{")) {
      // extract extensions from *.{md,mdx}
      const m = g.match(/\*\.\{([^}]+)\}/);
      if (m) return m[1].split(",").map(x=>"."+x.trim()).includes(ext);
    }
    return minimatch(rel, g);
  });
}
```

Simplest: define allowedExtensions in config or derive from includeGlobs
